Lessons.Title: Angle Measurement and Perpendicular Lines
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will practice using a protractor to measure angles and to learn that lines that intersect at a right angle are perpendicular lines.
In a previous lesson, you learned that a 1-degree angle measures a turn through ​ \(\frac{1}{360}\) ​ of a circle and that a protractor could be used to measure angles in degrees. In this lesson, you practice using a protractor to measure a variety of angles—angles formed by rays or line segments and those that are in other two-dimensional figures. Next, you are prompted to fold paper to create two lines that form right angles.

2021 lesson activities: Warm-up: Number Talk: Quotients (10 minutes); Activity 1: Angles Here, There, Everywhere (15 minutes); Activity 2: A Folding Challenge (20 minutes); Cool-down: Size Up Angles (5 minutes)
Corrected mathematical focus: Perpendicular lines intersect to form a 90° right angle; protractors measure the turn between two rays.

Edulytics authored guidance: Use a protractor to measure each labelled source angle with the zero baseline correctly aligned. Fold two creases through point P to create four right angles as the source challenge asks. Explain that their sum around P is 360°, so each is 90°.
First-party Cool-down (not publisher assessment): Draw two perpendicular straight lines, mark one of the four angles.
Images, drawing/protractor accuracy, partner tasks and the gated original publisher Cool-down require original task evidence and teacher/visual review.
